newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr hovers below 116 yen after trade data in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr hovers below 116 yen after trade data in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar was hovering below 116 yen at midday Tokyo on Monday after rebounding from dips following the release of Japan's trade data in early trading.

The dollar fell as low as 114.85 yen after the data was released, but soon recovered on buying back by interbank dealers and U.S. operators. By midday it remained top-heavy near 116 yen in thin trade, dealers said.
Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus more than doubled in April from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of friction, surged 174.1 percent in April from a year earlier to 468.97 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.

U.S. operators were said to have sold dollars initially after the release of the data and they were later joined by interbank dealers. But they were soon keen to buy back the greenback as the market digested the data, which was mostly in line with expectations.

A dealer at a city bank said that some Japanese investors were also behind the morning purchases, but others said they were still taking a wait-and-see stance. Some purchases by interbank dealers, possibly in connection with commercial buying at Japan's local fixing, were detected, pushing the dollar back close to 116 yen, a dealer a trust bank said.

Dealers said thin trade exaggerated the moves early on, but later in the morning dollar/yen trade was stuck in a narrow range amid a lack of fresh factors and ahead of a U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday and key U.S. economic data later this week.

But dealers added that some traders had started selling after confirming that the dollar's topside remained heavy near 116 yen. They said exporter offers and possible hedge sales by trust banks could emerge above 116 yen, weighing on the dollar, they said.
"There is still a downside risk below 115 yen," a trust bank dealer said.
But another trust bank dealer said: "The market is likely to remain thin (in the afternoon). But even if the dollar dips below 115 yen again, I think some Japanese investors will pick up the dollar."
In crosses, the mark firmed against the yen after setting off stop-loss purchases near 68.40 yen, a dealer at a European bank said.
But he added that some offers were expected near 68.70 yen, capping mark's gains.
